newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG, GOETSCHL DOMINATE TRAINING.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG, GOETSCHL DOMINATE TRAINING.

text.p: Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg and Austria's Renate Goetschl dominated training on Thursday ahead of Friday's World Cup downhill.

Goetschl, who registered her first career downhill victory in Vail, Colorado, two weeks ago, was quickest in the first of two training runs down the 1,880 metre Mont Lachaux course clocking a time of one minute 13.54 seconds.
Wiberg, locked in a battle with Germany's Katja Seizinger for the lead in the overall World Cup standings, was second in 1:14.05.
The two skiers switched places after their second trip down the slushy layout, Wiberg posting the day's fastest time of 1:13.40 followed closely by Goetschl with 1:13.45.
"I like this course very much, there are a lot of turns and it is very difficult," Goetschl said, "I feel strong enough that I could win here. My win in Vail has given me a lot of confidence."
Olympic downhill gold medallist Seizinger had problems with the soft conditions and could do no better than 19th in her first run and eighth in her second.
Friday's race will be the first women's World Cup downhill staged at the popular Swiss resort since 1986.
Germany's Katharina Gutensohn finished third in that race and a decade later found herself in the same place after posting the third fastest time in the opening training run.
